# Nutrition fundamentals — CI fixture

A balanced eating pattern includes a variety of vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, nuts, and suitable protein sources. Dietary needs vary with age, body size, activity, health status, and individual context.

Carbohydrates, fats, and protein provide energy and have different physiological roles. Protein contributes amino acids used to build and repair body tissues. Carbohydrate is an important fuel source during higher-intensity exercise. Dietary fats support essential functions, including absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.

Hydration needs vary with climate, exercise duration, sweat rate, and individual factors. Water intake should be adjusted to conditions rather than treated as one fixed amount for every person.

Nutrition guidance should be interpreted in context. A general educational document is not a substitute for individualized advice from a qualified healthcare professional.
